title: Web application
planning: Inspect the existing framework, package scripts, route conventions, design system, and neighboring components before choosing an implementation pattern.
Define one end-to-end user path before styling breadth. Keep server data access, validation, domain logic, and presentation at explicit boundaries.
Modify the canonical implementation instead of leaving copy, v1/v2/v3, test-page, or temporary variants in production paths.
Account for loading, empty, error, retry, narrow viewport, keyboard, and accessible-name states where the requested surface can encounter them.
Use shared request/response types or runtime schemas at network boundaries; do not spread untyped API payload assumptions through components.
checks: Run the repository's existing lint, typecheck, test, and production build commands; a dev-server render alone is insufficient.
Exercise the public browser path with realistic API success and failure responses, assert no console errors, and inspect the result at desktop and narrow widths.
Check that effects clean up, stale requests cannot overwrite newer state, non-2xx responses are handled before parsing, and loading always settles.
review: Reject duplicated components, speculative abstractions, placeholder production behavior, dead imports, broad any types, and comments that describe unfinished work.
Confirm the implementation follows the existing visual language instead of adding isolated inline styling or decorative motion not requested by the user.
